name: Ractopamine
health_effect: Tachycardia, heart palpitations, tremors, elevated blood pressure; cardiovascular contraindication; 218,000+ adverse pig events reported to FDA
banned_in_countries: EU, China, Russia, Taiwan, 160+ countries total
common_substitute_note: Certified ractopamine-free pork; USDA Organic beef/pork; Niman Ranch; White Oak Pastures
example_brands: Smithfield, Hormel, Tyson conventional pork; most US supermarket pork
time_to_manifest: Immediate in sensitive individuals; chronic cardiovascular risk months–years

name: Potassium Bromate
health_effect: IARC Group 2B carcinogen; kidney tumors, thyroid tumors, peritoneal mesothelioma in animal studies; DNA oxidative damage, renal failure
banned_in_countries: EU (1990), UK, Canada (1994), Brazil, China, South Korea, India (2016), Nigeria, Argentina, Peru; CA ban 2023; NY, UT school ban 2025
common_substitute_note: Ascorbic acid (vitamin C) as flour improver; unbromated flour (King Arthur, Bob's Red Mill)
found_in: Bread, rolls, bagels, pizza dough, flour
example_brands: Wonder Bread, many store-brand sandwich breads, some pizza chains

name: Azodicarbonamide
health_effect: Respiratory sensitizer; linked to liver and kidney tumors in animal studies (NTP 2025); degrades to semicarbazide (possible carcinogen) during baking
banned_in_countries: EU, Australia, Singapore, UK
common_substitute_note: Ascorbic acid; enzymes; calcium peroxide; naturally fermented/aged flour
example_brands: Subway bread (removed 2014), Sara Lee, some fast food buns

name: Erythrosine
health_effect: Thyroid tumors in animal studies; IARC Group 2B; caused cancer in rats at high doses — Delaney Clause triggered
banned_in_countries: EU (restricted); US (nationally banned Jan 15, 2025; phase-out by 2027–28); California (2023)
common_substitute_note: Natural red colorants: beet juice, anthocyanins, lycopene
found_in: Maraschino cherries, candy, some processed foods
example_brands: Maraschino cherries (most brands), some cake decorations

name: Brominated Vegetable Oil
health_effect: Neurological damage, headaches, memory loss, thyroid disruption; bromine accumulates in tissues
banned_in_countries: EU, Japan, India; US (FDA ban effective Aug 2, 2024)
common_substitute_note: Sucrose acetate isobutyrate (SAIB); ester gum
example_brands: Mountain Dew (removed), some store-brand citrus sodas

name: Titanium Dioxide
health_effect: Genotoxicity not ruled out; DNA/chromosomal damage possible; gut microbiome disruption; nanoparticle accumulation in brain (2025 Alzheimer's study); blood glucose disruption (mice, 2025)
banned_in_countries: EU (banned Feb 2022); Oman; voluntarily removed by many US brands
common_substitute_note: Natural white colorants: calcium carbonate, kaolin clay; reformulated products
found_in: Candy, chewing gum, coffee creamer, salad dressing, baked goods
example_brands: Skittles, Starburst, many white-colored processed foods

name: rBGH
health_effect: Elevated IGF-1 in milk linked to breast, prostate, colon cancer risk; increased mastitis in cows → antibiotic use
banned_in_countries: EU (banned 1990), Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, Norway
common_substitute_note: USDA Organic dairy; rBGH-free labeled milk (Organic Valley, Stonyfield, Cabot)
found_in: Conventional dairy: milk, cheese, yogurt, ice cream, butter
example_brands: Most conventional dairy brands (Kraft, Dean Foods); not in Organic Valley, Stonyfield, Horizon

name: Olestra
health_effect: GI cramping, diarrhea, fat-soluble vitamin depletion (A, D, E, K); appetite dysregulation in animal studies
banned_in_countries: EU, Canada, Australia; never sold in US since 2023
common_substitute_note: Real-food fat sources; avocado oil chips; air-popped popcorn
example_brands: Lay's WOW (discontinued); some store-brand "light" chips; effectively not sold in US since 2023

name: Propylparaben
health_effect: Endocrine disruptor; reproductive toxicity; disrupts estrogen signaling; fertility concerns
banned_in_countries: EU (withdrawn from food approval); California (banned 2023, effective 2027)
common_substitute_note: Vinegar-based preservation; ascorbic acid; potassium sorbate
example_brands: Some packaged tortillas, deli items, condiments

name: Methylparaben
health_effect: Weak estrogenic activity; endocrine disruption concern; cumulative exposure from food + cosmetics
banned_in_countries: NOTE: Propylparaben banned in EU food; Methyl/Ethylparaben still EU-approved with limits. Avoid all as precaution.
common_substitute_note: Vinegar; citric acid; rosemary extract; refrigeration
found_in: Bakery goods, dairy products, condiments, beverages
example_brands: Various packaged goods; cosmetics more commonly

name: BHT
health_effect: Endocrine disruption; tumor promotion in animal studies; reproductive harm; FDA postmarket safety review launched Aug 2025
banned_in_countries: EU (banned — endocrine concern); under FDA review 2025
common_substitute_note: Vitamin E (tocopherols); rosemary extract; no-preservative lines (Simple Mills, Annie's)
found_in: Cereals, crackers, snack foods, vegetable oils, packaging
example_brands: Wheat Thins, many breakfast cereals (Kellogg's, General Mills), Jiffy, Pillsbury

name: BHA
health_effect: IARC Group 2B carcinogen; CA Prop 65 listed; tumor promotion in animal studies; FDA ordered new safety review Feb 2026
banned_in_countries: Japan (banned 1982); EU (restricted); Under FDA safety review Feb 2026
common_substitute_note: Vitamin E (tocopherols); rosemary extract; clean-label oil alternatives
found_in: Vegetable oils, chips, cereals, gum, packaging
example_brands: Kellogg's cereals, Stouffer's, Jiffy Mix, some fast food oils

name: TBHQ
health_effect: Liver toxicity; immune disruption; potential food allergy amplification (Michigan State 2021); genotoxicity at high doses; stomach tumor precursors in animal studies
banned_in_countries: Japan (not approved — import rejections documented); EU permits at 0.02% limit
common_substitute_note: Vitamin E; rosemary extract; clean-label oils
found_in: Processed snack foods, oils, fast food
example_brands: Cheez-It, Pop-Tarts, McDonald's chicken nuggets (historically), many cooking oils

name: Cyclamates
health_effect: Bladder cancer in animal studies (basis for US ban); possible carcinogen
banned_in_countries: Banned in US since 1970; EU/Japan/Canada allow with limits
common_substitute_note: Stevia; monk fruit; erythritol
example_brands: Banned from US market since 1970; still in some Canadian/EU products

name: Chlorine Washes
health_effect: Controversial — residues considered low-risk; EU concern is it enables lower farm hygiene standards
banned_in_countries: EU (banned as poultry PRT since 1997)
common_substitute_note: Air-chilled poultry; organic chicken (no chlorine wash); EU-standard processing
example_brands: Most US supermarket chicken

name: Antibiotics in Animal Feed
health_effect: Antibiotic resistance; resistant bacteria transferable to humans via meat consumption; Salmonella, E. coli resistance strains documented
banned_in_countries: EU (banned for growth promotion 2006); Canada (restricted)
common_substitute_note: USDA Organic meat; antibiotic-free labeled products; ButcherBox; grass-fed beef
example_brands: Most conventional US meat

name: Growth Hormones in Beef
health_effect: Elevated estrogen/androgen residues; potential hormonal disruption; EU banned imports since 1989 on precautionary basis
banned_in_countries: EU (import ban since 1989 — ongoing WTO dispute)
common_substitute_note: USDA Organic beef; hormone-free labeled beef; grass-fed (American Grassfed Assoc.)
example_brands: Most US supermarket beef, fast food beef

name: Chlorpyrifos
health_effect: Neurotoxin; developmental neurotoxicity in children; cognitive impairment; EPA banned for food crops 2021
banned_in_countries: EU (2020), Canada, Australia; US EPA banned for food crop use 2021
common_substitute_note: USDA Organic produce; EWG Dirty Dozen guide; wash all produce thoroughly
example_brands: Non-organic produce at most retailers

name: Trans Fats
health_effect: Cardiovascular disease; raises LDL, lowers HDL; directly linked to heart attack risk; IARC Group 1
banned_in_countries: EU; Canada; Denmark (first, 2003); US FDA revoked GRAS status 2018
common_substitute_note: Butter; olive oil; avocado oil; coconut oil; palm oil (sustainable)
found_in: Margarine, shortening, fried foods, baked goods
example_brands: Crisco (reformulated), some restaurant frying oils, older packaged goods

name: Arsenic-based Drugs
health_effect: Inorganic arsenic in tissue; IARC Group 1 carcinogen (inorganic arsenic); kidney, bladder, skin cancer risk
banned_in_countries: EU; voluntarily withdrawn in US (Pfizer/Zoetis 2011–2015); not formally banned federally
common_substitute_note: Antibiotic/arsenic-free poultry; USDA Organic chicken
example_brands: Tyson (removed); most major producers removed voluntarily 2013–2015

name: Artificial Food Dyes
health_effect: Hyperactivity in children; possible ADHD exacerbation; neurobehavioral effects; 8% of children affected per some studies
banned_in_countries: EU requires black warning label "may affect activity and attention in children"; some countries restrict specific dyes; CA/UT/NY/PA moving to ban; no outright EU-wide ban
common_substitute_note: Beet juice; turmeric; spirulina; annatto; carrot juice; products using natural colors
example_brands: Skittles, M&Ms, Kool-Aid, Froot Loops, Gatorade

name: GMOs
health_effect: Long-term effects debated; EU precautionary principle applied; not proven harmful but lacks long-term human data
banned_in_countries: EU (cultivation restrictions in most member states; imports allowed with labeling); Russia (import ban); ~37 countries restrict cultivation
common_substitute_note: USDA Organic (no GMOs); Non-GMO Project verified products
found_in: Soy, corn, canola, sugar beet, alfalfa
example_brands: Most processed US food contains GMO soy/corn; Impossible Burger uses GMO soy

name: Phthalates
health_effect: Endocrine disruptors; reproductive toxicity; linked to lower testosterone; prenatal developmental harm
banned_in_countries: EU (restricted in food contact materials)
common_substitute_note: Glass or stainless containers; phthalate-free packaging; fresh unpackaged food
found_in: Food packaging, plastic wrap, some processing equipment
example_brands: Plastic-packaged meats, fast food, dairy in plastic packaging

name: PFOA
health_effect: Cancer (kidney, testicular); immune system disruption; thyroid disruption; liver damage; persist indefinitely in body and environment
banned_in_countries: EU (many restricted; PPWR packaging limits Feb 2025); multiple US states restricting
common_substitute_note: Stainless steel; cast iron; ceramic cookware; EU PPWR (Feb 2025) limits PFAS in packaging
found_in: Non-stick cookware coatings leaching; microwave popcorn bags; fast food wrappers; some drinking water
example_brands: Teflon-coated cookware; most microwave popcorn bags; many fast food packaging

name: Sodium Nitrite
health_effect: IARC Group 1: processed meat classified carcinogenic (colorectal cancer); N-nitroso compound formation; nitrosamine formation during cooking
banned_in_countries: Not banned; EU lowered permitted levels 2023; WHO IARC Group 1 for processed meat
common_substitute_note: Nitrate-free/uncured meats; fresh meat; Applegate Naturals; Aidells; home-cooked fresh protein
found_in: Processed meats: hot dogs, bacon, ham, deli meats, sausages
example_brands: Oscar Mayer hot dogs, Applegate (uses natural sources), most deli meats
time_to_manifest: Years of regular processed meat consumption

name: Aspartame
health_effect: IARC Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic) July 2023; neuropsychiatric effects at high doses; headaches; contraindicated in phenylketonuria; possible lymphoma/myeloma link
banned_in_countries: EU (Saccharin restricted); aspartame itself not banned anywhere; IARC Group 2B flagged July 2023; WHO/JECFA kept ADI unchanged
common_substitute_note: Stevia; monk fruit; erythritol; minimal added sugar
found_in: Diet sodas, sugar-free products, chewing gum, yogurts
example_brands: Diet Coke, Diet Pepsi, Coke Zero, Equal, NutraSweet

name: Carrageenan
health_effect: Gut inflammation; linked to colitis and IBS in animal studies; intestinal permeability concerns
banned_in_countries: EU (banned in infant formula only); IARC review ongoing
common_substitute_note: Carrageenan-free nut milks (some Califia Farms); whole-food plant milks; certified carrageenan-free products
found_in: Plant-based milks, infant formula, deli meats, cottage cheese
example_brands: Silk almond milk (some products), many conventional dairy alternatives

name: Polysorbate 80
health_effect: Gut microbiome disruption; metabolic syndrome in mice; intestinal permeability; emulsification of gut lining
banned_in_countries: None — widely approved; emerging research only
common_substitute_note: Sunflower lecithin; mustard flour; guar gum; products labeled "no emulsifiers"
found_in: Ice cream, pickles, vitamins, vaccines, processed sauces
example_brands: Häagen-Dazs (some flavors), many packaged ice creams, condiments

name: Acrylamide
health_effect: IARC Group 2A (probably carcinogenic); linked to endometrial, ovarian cancer in women; DNA damage
banned_in_countries: None — EU benchmark regulation levels; not banned
common_substitute_note: Lower-temperature cooking; steaming; boiling; avoid burnt/very dark toast or fries
found_in: Fried/baked starchy foods at high heat
example_brands: French fries, potato chips, coffee, toast, breakfast cereals

name: High-Fructose Corn Syrup
health_effect: Obesity; type 2 diabetes; fatty liver disease; elevated LDL; accelerated glycation; does not trigger satiety signals normally
banned_in_countries: None — not a regulatory ban issue; EU uses HFCS less due to sugar quotas (economic, not safety)
common_substitute_note: Pure cane sugar (in moderation); water; whole fruit; beverages sweetened with stevia/monk fruit
found_in: Sodas, candy, sweetened cereals, condiments, salad dressings
example_brands: Coca-Cola, Pepsi, most US sodas; Heinz ketchup; most US bread

name: Partially Hydrogenated Oils
health_effect: Same as trans fats — direct cardiovascular disease link
banned_in_countries: EU; Canada; Denmark (first ban 2003); US FDA GRAS revoked 2018
common_substitute_note: Real butter; olive oil; avocado oil; coconut oil
example_brands: Crisco (reformulated); some bakery products; restaurant frying oil (largely phased out)

name: Sulfites
health_effect: Asthma attacks in sensitive individuals; anaphylaxis in sulfite-sensitive people; WHO estimated 1% population sensitive
banned_in_countries: EU (restricted to maximum levels); FDA requires labeling if >10ppm; not a full ban
common_substitute_note: Sulfite-free wine; unsulfured dried fruit; fresh produce
found_in: Dried fruit, wine, processed potatoes, condiments
example_brands: Sun-Maid raisins, most wine, some deli salads

name: Glyphosate Residues
health_effect: IARC Group 2A (probably carcinogenic); potential endocrine disruption; gut microbiome disruption; billions in Roundup litigation settlements
banned_in_countries: NOT banned in EU (approved to Dec 2033 with use restrictions; some municipalities restrict locally); Sri Lanka ban (2015) largely reversed 2018
common_substitute_note: USDA Organic grains and cereals; certified glyphosate-free products
found_in: Conventionally grown grains, soy, oats, beans, legumes
example_brands: Quaker Oats (residues detected by EWG); many conventional grain products

name: Pesticide Residues on Produce
health_effect: Neurotoxicity; endocrine disruption; cancer risk depending on specific pesticide; children most vulnerable
banned_in_countries: EU restricts specific pesticides with MRLs (maximum residue levels); complex per-chemical regulation
common_substitute_note: USDA Organic produce; EWG Clean Fifteen guide; thorough washing
example_brands: Most non-organic produce; EWG Dirty Dozen: strawberries, spinach, kale, peaches, pears, nectarines

name: Ethoxyquin
health_effect: Liver toxicity; carcinogenicity concern; thyroid disruption; EU suspended use due to data gaps 2017
banned_in_countries: EU (suspended food use 2017); Japan
common_substitute_note: Wild-caught salmon; ethoxyquin-free pet food (The Honest Kitchen, Orijen)
found_in: Pet food; fish meal used in farmed salmon
example_brands: Some farmed salmon products; most commercial pet food

name: Cadmium in Imported Seafood
health_effect: Kidney damage; bone demineralization; IARC Group 1 carcinogen; accumulates in kidneys over decades
banned_in_countries: EU, Japan (both set maximum limits)
common_substitute_note: Wild-caught domestic fish; MSC-certified seafood; limit shellfish from high-contamination zones
example_brands: Mussels, oysters, kidneys from some imported products

name: Lead in Imported Candy/Spices
health_effect: Neurotoxicity especially in children; cognitive impairment; no safe level; developmental harm
banned_in_countries: EU, Canada (strict maximum limits); FDA import alerts on recurring violators
common_substitute_note: Domestic-sourced spices; tested spice brands (Simply Organic, Frontier Co-op)
example_brands: Some Mexican candy (historically); certain imported spice blends

name: Mercury in Processed/Canned Fish
health_effect: Neurotoxicity; developmental harm in fetuses/children; kidney damage; methylmercury bioaccumulates
banned_in_countries: EU, Japan (maximum limits by species); FDA advisory (not a ban)
common_substitute_note: Canned salmon; sardines; light tuna (lower mercury); wild Alaska pollock
example_brands: Canned albacore/chunk light tuna (Starkist, Bumble Bee); swordfish; shark; king mackerel

name: Melamine in Imported Products
health_effect: Kidney stones; kidney failure; urinary tract cancer; 300,000+ children affected in 2008 China scandal
banned_in_countries: EU, China (post-scandal strict limits); international MRLs in place
common_substitute_note: Domestic dairy; certified suppliers; avoid counterfeit or unverified imports
found_in: Imported dairy, infant formula, some processed foods
example_brands: Chinese dairy products (2008 scandal); some imported processed products

name: Fluoroquinolones in Chicken
health_effect: Antibiotic resistance; resistant Campylobacter in humans from poultry exposure
banned_in_countries: EU; China; US FDA banned for poultry use in 2005 (US led this ban)
common_substitute_note: USDA Organic poultry; antibiotic-free labeled chicken
example_brands: Historical issue with many US brands — now largely resolved

name: Farmed Salmon Additives
health_effect: Synthetic astaxanthin from petrochemical sources; antibiotic residues; PCB concentration higher than wild
banned_in_countries: EU (restricts specific antibiotics and synthetic colorant levels)
common_substitute_note: Wild-caught Alaskan/Pacific salmon; MSC-certified; Vital Choice brand
example_brands: Most supermarket farmed Atlantic salmon (Costco, many grocery chains)

name: Ammonia-treated Meat
health_effect: Residual ammonia; nutritional dilution; consumer deception concern; not definitively proven harmful in itself
banned_in_countries: None — USDA approved; EU's chlorine wash ban effectively also limits this
common_substitute_note: 100% grass-fed ground beef; butcher-sourced ground beef; full-muscle cuts
found_in: Ground beef, some processed meat products
example_brands: Previously in McDonald's, Burger King (removed ~2012); still some retail ground beef

name: Meat Glue
health_effect: Microbiological risk (bacteria trapped inside); allergen cross-contamination; consumer deception
banned_in_countries: EU (mandatory labeling "formed meat" required)
common_substitute_note: Whole-muscle cuts; unprocessed fresh meat
found_in: Restaurant steaks, processed deli meats, restructured meat products
example_brands: Some restaurant "steaks"; deli meat blocks

name: Propylene Glycol
health_effect: Liver toxicity in cats; low human toxicity at food-grade levels; GRAS in US but limited in some uses
banned_in_countries: None in human food; EU restricts in some applications
common_substitute_note: Vegetable glycerin; natural emulsifiers; products without this additive
found_in: Salad dressings, bread, pet food, some ice cream
example_brands: Some flavored beverages; certain bread products; many pet foods

name: Sodium Benzoate
health_effect: Combines with ascorbic acid to form benzene (carcinogen) in acidic beverages; hyperactivity at high doses
banned_in_countries: None (banned in some countries in infant formula); EU regulates maximum levels
common_substitute_note: Refrigeration-based preservation; vinegar; citric acid; beverages without preservatives
example_brands: Diet Coke, Pepsi products, many juices, soy sauce

name: Caramel Coloring
health_effect: 4-MEI (4-methylimidazole) — CA Prop 65 listed carcinogen; IARC Group 2B
banned_in_countries: None outright; California requires Prop 65 warning for certain levels
common_substitute_note: Natural caramel (Class I/II); no color additives; products without artificial color
found_in: Sodas, beer, soy sauce, some baked goods
example_brands: Coca-Cola, Pepsi (use Class IV); most dark-colored sodas

name: Formaldehyde
health_effect: IARC Group 1 carcinogen (via inhalation primarily); food route exposure much lower; kidney/liver damage at high levels
banned_in_countries: EU (restricted in food use/packaging)
common_substitute_note: Fresh unprocessed foods; glass-packaged products
example_brands: Some smoked meats, certain imported preserved foods

name: Sulfur Dioxide
health_effect: Asthma trigger; anaphylaxis in sensitive people; destroys thiamine (B1)
banned_in_countries: EU (restricted to maximum levels, E220)
common_substitute_note: Sulfite-free/organic wine; unsulfured dried fruit; fresh fruit
found_in: Wine, dried fruits, some fruit juices
example_brands: Most commercial wine, Sun-Maid raisins, many dried apricots

name: Nitrosamines in Smoked Foods
health_effect: IARC Group 2A carcinogens; colorectal, gastric, esophageal cancer risk
banned_in_countries: EU (restricted levels)
common_substitute_note: Unsmoked alternatives; liquid smoke (lower nitrosamine); fresh protein
found_in: Smoked/cured meats, smoked fish, some beers
example_brands: Smoked sausages, some smoked cheeses, nitrite-cured smoked products

name: Aluminum Compounds in Baking Powder
health_effect: Neurotoxicity at high exposure; Alzheimer's associations (contested); kidney accumulation
banned_in_countries: EU (restricts aluminum migration limits in food)
common_substitute_note: Aluminum-free baking powder (Rumford, Bob's Red Mill); cream of tartar; non-processed cheese
found_in: Pancake mixes, baking powder, processed cheese
example_brands: Rumford (aluminum-free available); some store-brand baking powder; American cheese slices

name: Caramel Coloring III/IV
health_effect: As above — 4-MEI concern
banned_in_countries: CA Prop 65 threshold
common_substitute_note: Natural alternatives; color-free products
example_brands: Coca-Cola, Pepsi, most cola drinks globally

name: Monosodium Glutamate
health_effect: Headache, flushing in some people (debated — "Chinese restaurant syndrome" not conclusively proven); excitotoxicity concerns at very high doses
banned_in_countries: None — GRAS in US; EFSA-approved in EU; no country bans it
common_substitute_note: Real salt, herbs and spices, tamari, nutritional yeast for umami flavor
found_in: Chinese food, chips, canned soups, processed snacks
example_brands: Doritos, many ramen brands, Campbell's soups, KFC

name: Synthetic Flavoring Agents
health_effect: Undisclosed chemical combinations; some linked to respiratory harm in workers; consumer has no transparency
banned_in_countries: None — regulated by FEMA GRAS list in US; not banned
common_substitute_note: Products listing real, named ingredients; whole foods; cook from scratch
example_brands: Most packaged snack foods; fast food

name: Natural Flavor
health_effect: Undisclosed — can mask hundreds of individual chemicals under one label; no transparency
banned_in_countries: None — a labeling classification, not a substance
common_substitute_note: Products listing actual ingredient sources by name
example_brands: Ubiquitous — almost any packaged product

name: Synthetic Vanillin
health_effect: Liver stress at very high doses (animal studies); not a primary concern at food-use levels
banned_in_countries: None
common_substitute_note: Pure vanilla extract (McCormick Pure, Nielsen-Massey)
found_in: Flavored beverages, baked goods, ice cream
example_brands: Imitation vanilla extract products; most mass-market cookies

name: Calcium Propionate
health_effect: Behavioral effects in children debated; migraine trigger in some adults; animal studies show some cellular effects
banned_in_countries: None
common_substitute_note: Home-baked bread; sourdough (acetic acid-preserved); clean-label bakeries
example_brands: Wonder Bread, most commercial sandwich bread

name: Sorbates
health_effect: Genotoxicity reported in some in vitro studies; generally regarded as low-concern; can convert to sorbic acid
banned_in_countries: None
common_substitute_note: Refrigeration; lacto-fermented preservation; ascorbic acid
found_in: Wine, cheese, baked goods, deli items
example_brands: Most commercial cheeses, some wines, packaged salads

name: Dimethylpolysiloxane
health_effect: Limited human safety data; siloxane residues; not studied at food exposure levels adequately
banned_in_countries: None
common_substitute_note: Avoidance of repeated deep-fried fast food; home cooking
found_in: Cooking oils, fast food fryers, nonstick agents
example_brands: McDonald's frying oil (still used as anti-foaming agent)

name: Butane
health_effect: Inhalation risk (abuse potential); negligible food-contact exposure concern at normal use
banned_in_countries: None
common_substitute_note: Pump-spray olive oil dispensers; pour-from-bottle oils
found_in: Aerosol cooking sprays, whipped cream canisters
example_brands: PAM cooking spray; canned whipped cream

name: Propylene Glycol Esters
health_effect: Low acute toxicity; limited long-term human data
banned_in_countries: None
common_substitute_note: Home-baked goods; clean-label alternatives
found_in: Baked goods, cake mixes, whipped toppings
example_brands: Betty Crocker, Pillsbury cake mixes; Cool Whip

name: Non-Organic Wax Coatings
health_effect: Shellac (insect-derived); petroleum-based waxes; pesticide trapping under wax; difficult to wash off
banned_in_countries: None — requires disclosure in US
common_substitute_note: Buy organic; peel waxed produce; farmers market uncoated produce
example_brands: Most non-organic produce at major retailers

name: Sodium Erythorbate
health_effect: Used with nitrites — may affect nitrosamine formation; not independently harmful at food levels
banned_in_countries: None
common_substitute_note: Nitrate-free meats; fresh protein sources
example_brands: Oscar Mayer hot dogs, most commercial deli meats

name: Potassium Lactate
health_effect: Generally regarded as safe; can affect sodium intake; minimal independent health concern
banned_in_countries: None
common_substitute_note: Fresh unprocessed meats
example_brands: Many commercial deli products

name: Perchlorate
health_effect: Thyroid function interference; iodine uptake disruption; developmental risk in fetuses/infants
banned_in_countries: No specific ban in OECD countries; EPA regulates in drinking water
common_substitute_note: Filtered water (reverse osmosis); organic produce in low-contamination regions
example_brands: Lettuce, spinach, dairy from contaminated pastures

name: Hexane
health_effect: Neurotoxin at occupational exposure levels; residues in food are very low; long-term concern at food levels unclear
banned_in_countries: None; FDA/EU set maximum residue limits
common_substitute_note: Expeller-pressed or cold-pressed oils (Spectrum, Bragg); organic soy protein
example_brands: Most US soy protein products; many vegetable oils

name: Caffeine in Energy Drinks
health_effect: Cardiovascular stress; hypertension; anxiety; sleep disruption; arrhythmias at high doses; pediatric deaths documented at extreme doses
banned_in_countries: None outright; EU recommends 400mg/day maximum
common_substitute_note: Green tea; matcha; herbal adaptogen drinks; low-caffeine alternatives
example_brands: Red Bull, Monster, Celsius, 5-hour Energy

name: Excessive Food Acidity Regulators
health_effect: Concern category — depends entirely on specific acid used
banned_in_countries: Concern category — not a specific banned substance
common_substitute_note: Whole foods
example_brands: Broad category — see phosphate additives

name: Excessive Salt
health_effect: Hypertension; cardiovascular disease; stroke
banned_in_countries: None — concern category only
common_substitute_note: Home cooking with herbs/spices; low-sodium labeled products
found_in: Virtually all processed and fast food
example_brands: Broad category

name: Refined Sugars
health_effect: Obesity; diabetes; dental caries; inflammation; metabolic syndrome
banned_in_countries: None
common_substitute_note: Whole fruit; small amounts of honey or maple syrup
example_brands: White sugar, cane sugar, dextrose, corn syrup

name: Excessive Omega-6 Oils
health_effect: Systemic inflammation; HDL suppression; promotes inflammatory arachidonic acid cascade
banned_in_countries: None
common_substitute_note: Olive oil; avocado oil; coconut oil; butter; ghee
example_brands: Vegetable oil, soybean oil, canola oil, sunflower oil in most packaged products

name: Emulsifiers in Processed Foods
health_effect: Gut microbiome disruption; intestinal permeability (emerging research)
banned_in_countries: None
common_substitute_note: Whole unprocessed foods
example_brands: Concern category

name: High Fluoride in Water
health_effect: Dental and skeletal fluorosis at high levels; US HHS lowered recommended level 2025
banned_in_countries: None — water policy, not food additive
common_substitute_note: Filtered water; spring water; reverse osmosis
